implemented: ZIP compression flush after authorized entry payload, first entry immediately and subsequent entries at most once per 250ms.
Flush archive and HTTP buffers together; X-Accel-Buffering: no disables nginx buffering for ZIP responses.
Check request cancellation between ZIP copy reads.
Record client headers and first body-byte timings in beta validation.

validation.targetedRaceTests: passed, 2.854s server; streaming payload gate, ZIP CRC/output, cancellation, integration ZIP and shared cache/HTTP paths
validation.decodedContentAndCRC: passed; repeated ZIP bytes identical within each run

tradeoffs: Sync flush slightly increases ZIP size.
Authorization remains per-entry and serial; this reduces initial body latency, not total authorization work.
A partial ZIP cannot be opened as a complete archive until its central directory arrives.
Entry copies are synchronous and respect transport backpressure; no producer queue or archive-sized memory buffer added.

remainingFindings.finding: Worker spools input, processes whole-file regex, and publishes output before serving. Generic chunking can change regex matches or leak boundary-spanning terms. A streaming fast path needs a provably bounded pattern subset.
ZIP loads up to 100000 file rows before streaming. A Mongo cursor with projection would reduce metadata memory and preparation latency; name collision detection must remain.
Cached gzip results are decoded and recompressed for ZIP. Raw deflate reuse could reduce CPU, but needs gzip-header/trailer, CRC and size validation plus corruption tests.
Server has a two-minute absolute write deadline. Consider bounded idle write deadlines for long active streams, retaining protection from stalled clients.

methodology: Three sequential samples per deployment through https://beta.durieux.me. Existing source caches may be warm. Client firstBodyByteMs measures actual body arrival, not only response headers. Not a load test.
